messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing & economics: AcmeAI dedicated lanes — next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so we can model a small dedicated pilot that matches your latency and budget objectives.

Recap of what I heard on the call:
- Workload: customer-facing summarization + follow-up Q&A for enterprise docs. Mostly long-form generation.
- Typical interaction: ~600 token prompt + ~1,200 token response (approx 1.8k tokens per request).
- Expected steady-state: ~3k–5k requests/day initially (roughly 5.4M–9M tokens/day; ~160M–270M tokens/month if steady).
- Peak concurrency: short bursts up to ~35 concurrent inferences during daytime windows.
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <= 600ms for the user-facing flow.
- Timeline: pilot procurement in ~6 weeks; aim to go live with pilot in Q3.

Key qualification asks for the sizing model (can you confirm):
1) Tokens per request: is 1.8k a fair average (prompt+response)?
2) Expected monthly tokens for the pilot: do you expect 100M–250M range or something different?
3) Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of ~$300 per 1M tokens during pilot — is that the floor you need, or negotiable with committed capacity?
4) GPU preference: you said H100 preferred for latency-sensitive ranking; are you open to a mixed H100/A100 lane if it materially changes cost?

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- Camila will produce a throughput matrix showing 2/4/8 reserved-GPU SKUs (H100 and A100 options) with modeled p95 latency and an estimated $/1M tokens for each SKU. Expect that by EOD tomorrow.
- We’ll attach a short pricing packet and a throughput workbook for you to review (attached).
- If the unit econ target is firm, we’ll also run a quick configuration that trades latency for cost (e.g., slightly higher batch sizes, quantization) to hit the target.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing packet), throughput_modeling_acme.csv (baseline throughput model).

If anything above is off, flag it and we’ll adjust before Camila runs the modeling. Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the numbers once we have the matrix.

Thanks,
Markus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Pilot sizing & economics: AcmeAI dedicated lanes — next steps

Thanks Markus — this is very helpful. Confirming the numbers from our side with a bit more color: 

- Tokens per request: yes, 1.8k average is our current estimate (will vary by prompt, but that's the right ballpark).
- Monthly tokens: for the initial pilot we expect 80M–140M tokens (we ramp during pilot, target ~120M/month mid-pilot).
- Concurrency: peak bursts are short-lived; 30–40 concurrent calls is realistic during demos/peak windows.
- Latency: p95 <= 700ms acceptable for pilot; <600ms preferred.
- Unit economics: procurement has sign-off for a pilot if the blended cost is <= $300 per 1M tokens. If the pilot requires higher commit, we could look at $275–320 with a larger reserved commitment.
- GPUs: we prefer H100 for the generative quality and latency profile but would consider A100 if it reduces unit cost significantly and latency stays within the pilot p95 target.

Procurement timeline: we expect a PO within 4–8 weeks after we confirm SKUs and pricing.

One more ask — can you include an explicit $/1M tokens for both: (A) 4x H100 reserved baseline and (B) 8x A100 reserved baseline, with an assumed monthly token volume of 120M? That will make internal approval much easier.

Appreciate it,
Alice Cheng
Head of Integrations | AcmeAI
alice.cheng@acmeai.com

Alice — thanks for the quick confirmation. Camila and I ran a first-pass sizing overnight and attached the workbook. High-level numbers for the specific asks you made (assumes 120M tokens/month):

Option A — 4x H100 reserved (baseline, single-region US):
- Modeled steady throughput: supports ~35 concurrent requests with p95 ~ 580ms (1.8k tokens/request).
- Estimated blended unit cost: ~$265 per 1M tokens (includes reserved capacity amortized + burst allowance + infra premium).
- Monthly platform fee + reserved GPU amortization: $78,000/month (not including overage).

Option B — 8x A100 reserved (cost-optimized, single-region US):
- Modeled steady throughput: supports ~60 concurrent requests; p95 ~ 720ms (slightly above your preferred, but within pilot tolerance).
- Estimated blended unit cost: ~$215 per 1M tokens.
- Monthly platform fee + reserved GPU amortization: $92,000/month (A100 cheaper per-GPU but requires more units to match throughput).

Notes and tradeoffs:
- H100 option hits your p95 < 600ms target and gives headroom for QPS spikes; it comes at higher per-month reserved cost but better unit econ when latency SLO matters.
- A100 option is more cost-efficient on $/1M tokens but trades a bit on p95 latency; if you can tolerate p95 ~ 700ms we can tune batching/kv-cache to tighten that.
- We modeled a hybrid lane (2x H100 + 4x A100) as a middle ground: ~ $235 per 1M tokens and p95 ~ 620ms. See the attached throughput_modeling_acme.csv for the full matrix.

Requested next steps:
1) Camila: can you validate the burst-headroom assumptions (I flagged two spots in the CSV where we assume 40% burst capacity)?
2) Alice: if the $265 (H100) or $215 (A100) numbers look directionally right, we can sketch a simple 6–8 week pilot SOW and prepare a PO template for procurement.
3) Lauren: FYI — this deal is approaching our mid-market reserved SKU approval for a one-off pilot discount. I’ll post the exact discount ask once we decide SKU.

I’ve attached: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing packet) and throughput_modeling_acme.csv (detailed latency/throughput matrix).

If helpful I can hop on a short call with procurement + Camila to walk through the workbook.

Thanks,
Markus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
